main_body: A 4x3-tile farm ground patch: a wheat/crop band on top, a green leafy hedge row below it, then tilled brown soil furrows with sprouts. It is drawn flat as ground, not as a standing object.
top_band: none. This is a ground/terrain patch, so there is no standing top band over a front face. The column scan shows stacked horizontal crop, leaf and soil bands.
evidence: The kind is terrain (ground tiles), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. The patch has no side faces and does not read as an upright elevation. Its rows of crops, sprouts and furrows suit a ground tile, so I do not fail it on projection.

style.evidence: Each material has several tones. The wheat band runs from cream and bright yellow through gold to brown. The leaves run from #73b83e through #58a035 and #4b8232 to the deep green #205030. The soil has about five browns with lighter clod dots. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or green, i.e. material tone. 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, with pixel-level texture and sprout tufts throughout. The median of 13 colours per tile is below the grass reference (26) but above the paving reference (7). The 24 total colours are far fewer than grass (80), so density is slightly lower, yet it reads as crafted and not like a sticker next to the references.
